title: Burkina Faso Holds Rally to Mark Traore Coup Anniversary
excerpt: Thousands of supporters of Burkina Faso’s military government gathered overnight in the capital, Ouagadougou, and other parts of the country to mark the fourth anniversary of the coup that brought Captain Ibrahim Traore to power. The rally, organised at the initiative of the junta, began at 6 pm on Wednesday and was described by organisers as a vigil celebrating Traore’s “Popular Progressive Revolution”. The 38-year-old military leader seized power in a September 2022 coup and has since presented himself as a Pan-African figure opposing Western influence on the continent. The anniversary events were broadcast on state television and continued into the night, with concerts featuring artists praising the military government and its record in power. Many participants carried posters bearing Traore’s image. When he assumed power, Traore pledged to end the terrorist violence that has affected Burkina Faso since 2015, promising to restore security within months. title: Lutte contre la fraude et l’orpaillage clandestin: Condor Autorité et ses hommes frappent fort
translated_title: Fight against fraud and clandestine gold mining: Condor Authority and its men strike hard
excerpt: L’Unité Combattante des Eaux et Forêts basée à Djikologo (Djôrô, ex-sud-ouest burkinabè) a mené, du 26 au 27 septembre 2026, une série d’opérations contre les trafics illicites, la fraude et l’orpaillage clandestin. Ces opérations ont permis d’obtenir des résultats significatifs, illustrant la détermination des agents à protéger les ressources naturelles, à préserver l’environnement et à faire respecter la loi. 35 tonnes d’amandes de karité saisies Le samedi 26 septembre 2026, les éléments de l’Unité ont intercepté et saisi, sur l’axe Djikologo-Dissine, un camion-remorque transportant environ 35 tonnes d’amandes de karité. title: Mali: more than 2,400 schools remain closed as insecurity disrupts new school year
excerpt: Mali's new school year began Thursday with more than 2,400 schools unable to reopen, as worsening insecurity and the growing presence of jihadist groups continue to disrupt education. The 2026-2027 academic year has been declared the “Year of Education and Culture” by President Assimi Goïta, but thousands of children are starting the year without access to their classrooms. According to figures from Mali's Education Ministry, the number of closed schools has continued to rise in recent years as violence spreads across parts of the country. The closures are affecting communities already facing displacement and disruption from the conflict, leaving children with fewer opportunities to continue their education. The government has made education a priority, but the security situation remains a major obstacle to reopening schools in affected areas. As the new academic year begins, the challenge for Mali is not only to get children back into classrooms, but also to ensure that schools can remain open and safe despite the continuing insecurity.
article_summary: Mali's new school year began Thursday with more than 2,400 schools unable to reopen, as worsening insecurity and the growing presence of jihadist groups continue to disrupt education. title: Bandits abduct 47 Niger women, others harvesting groundnuts
excerpt: By Clare Nnabuike, Minna MINNA — No fewer than 47 people, mostly women, have been abducted by suspected bandits while harvesting groundnuts on farms in Mariga Local Government Area of Niger State. The incident occurred on Saturday at Tungan Rimi in Ma’undu-Beri Ward of the council area. The victims were said to have been working on their farms when the armed men invaded the area and took them into the forest. The Chairman of Mariga Local Government Area, Alhaji Aliyu Bagga Muhamadu, confirmed the incident, saying the victims comprised mostly women and a few men. He disclosed that one of the abducted women reportedly gave birth while in captivity. According to him, the bandits had contacted relatives of the victims and were demanding a ransom of N2 million for each person. Muhamadu said joint security operatives and local vigilantes had moved into the forest in an effort to rescue the victims. article_summary: By Clare Nnabuike, Minna MINNA — No fewer than 47 people, mostly women, have been abducted by suspected bandits while harvesting groundnuts on farms in Mariga Local Government Area of Niger State. Notons qu’en dehors des plaquettes de cocaïne, les gendarmes ont également saisi un véhicule de marque Toyota, trois téléphones portables de type Android de marques Samsung

title: Burkina Faso Opens First Gold Refinery
excerpt: Burkina Faso Opens First Gold Refinery Burkina Faso has opened its first gold refinery as the military-led government seeks greater control over the country's mineral wealth and to reduce its reliance on exporting raw materials. The Raffinor-BF facility in Ouagadougou cost more than $19 million and has a refining capacity of 164 tonnes of gold per year, with plans to eventually increase capacity to 515 tonnes. The government said that the refinery will help regulate the informal mining sector, curb smuggling and keep more value from gold production within the country. The project is part of Captain Ibrahim Traoré's broader push for greater state involvement in mining and domestic processing. The government has also linked illegal gold trading to the financing of Islamist armed groups. title: Mali: Mali Army and Russian Fighters Accused of Killing Dozens of Civilians
excerpt: Mali's armed forces and Russian Wagner Group personnel committed war crimes including killings and torture of civilians during joint operations between 2023 and 2025, Amnesty International has said in a new report documenting abuses across several regions of the country. At least 34 civilians were killed in seven locations in the central Ségou and Mopti regions and northern Timbuktu region between June 2023 and December 2025, Amnesty said. None of those killed was directly participating in hostilities at the time, the rights organisation said. Some were shot while attempting to flee or after being arrested, while others had their throats slit or were burnt alive or after their deaths. The report - entitled No One is Spared - also documents torture, enforced disappearances, looting and two drone strikes that Amnesty says killed at least 23 civilians, including five children. The west African nation is the continent's third leading gold producer, churning out more than 94 tonnes of the precious metal last year, according to the World Gold Council. But authorities traditionally struggle to control the informal gold mining sector, which has been blighted by jihadist violence and smuggling. title: Amnesty Report Accuses Mali Army, Wagner Group of War Crimes
excerpt: Amnesty Report Accuses Mali Army, Wagner Group of War Crimes A new report by Amnesty International has accused the Malian army and the Russian-backed Wagner Group of committing war crimes during joint operations between 2023 and 2025. The report, No One Is Spared: War Crimes Committed by the Malian Army and Foreign Allied Forces Along the Mauritanian Border, documents the killing of at least 34 civilians across seven areas in Mali between June 2023 and December 2025. ''The Malian authorities cannot dismiss these serious allegations without opening impartial and effective investigations into the alleged crimes,'' said Marceau Sivieude, Amnesty International's Regional Director for West and Central Africa. The campaign group has urged the warring parties to protect civilians during military operations and comply with international humanitarian law, calling on authorities to ''urgently clarify the chain of command under which foreign personnel act in the country, and monitor their conduct through an independent, domestic accountability mechanism". InFocus - The latest Human Rights Watch
article_summary: A new report by Amnesty International has accused the Malian army and the Russian-backed Wagner Group of committing war crimes during joint operations between 2023 and 2025. The report, No One Is Spared: War Crimes Committed by the Malian Army and Foreign Allied Forces Along the Mauritanian Border, documents the killing of at least 34 civilians across seven areas in Mali between June 2023 and December 2025.

title: Burkina Faso opens first-ever gold refinery
excerpt: Burkina Faso opened its first gold refinery on Monday, pushing ahead with plans to better organise the commercialisation of the precious metal in one of the continent’s top producers. The West African nation is the continent’s third leading gold producer, churning out more than 94 tonnes of the precious metal last year, according to the World Gold Council. But authorities traditionally struggle to control the informal gold mining sector, which has been blighted by jihadist violence and smuggling. “Burkina Faso has reached a historic milestone in its quest for economic independence,” the presidency said in a statement. Under Captain Ibrahim Traore, who seized power in a 2022 coup, Burkina Faso has nationalised several gold mines and launched a push to revitalise the country’s industrial output, from cotton to tomatoes and textiles. title: Ségou : Une trentaine de terroristes du JNIM et du FLA neutralisés par les FAMa et l'Africa Corps
translated_title: Segou: About thirty JNIM and Fla terrorists neutralized by the FAMa and the Africa Corps
excerpt: Ségou : Une trentaine de terroristes du JNIM et du FLA neutralisés par les FAMa et l'Africa Corps Une opération militaire conjointe menée par l'Africa Corps des Forces armées de la Fédération de Russie et les Forces armées maliennes (FAMa) a abouti, ce dimanche, à la destruction d'un important groupe terroriste dans la région de Ségou. Selon les informations relayées par l'Africa Corps, l'engagement a ciblé une coalition de combattants affiliés au Front de Libération de l'Azawad (FLA) et au Groupe de soutien à l'islam et aux musulmans (JNIM). Le bilan provisoire de l'opération fait état d'une trentaine de terroristes éliminés. Les forces conjointes ont également saisi 20 armes de petit calibre ainsi qu'une quantité importante de munitions sur le site des affrontements. Cette action s'inscrit dans le cadre de la poursuite des opérations de sécurisation du centre du pays, témoignant d'une coordination renforcée entre les forces maliennes et leurs partenaires russes sur le terrain. T.Sindy/Malijet.com
translated_excerpt: Ségou: About thirty JNIM and Fla terrorists neutralized by the FAMa and the Africa Corps A joint military operation led by the Africa Corps of the Armed Forces of the Russian Federation and the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa) resulted, this Sunday, in the destruction of a large terrorist group in the Ségou region According to information relayed by the Africa Corps, the engagement targeted a coalition of fighters affiliated with the Azawad Liberation Front (Fla) and the Group for the Support of Islam and Muslims (JNIM). The provisional assessment of the operation shows that about thirty terrorists have been eliminated. The joint forces also seized 20 small arms as well as a significant amount of ammunition at the site of the clashes . This action is part of the ongoing security operations in the centre of the country, demonstrating enhanced coordination between the Malian forces and their Russian partners on the ground. T.Sindy/Malijet.com

title: Traoré marks four years in power, following Sankara’s legacy
excerpt: Captain Ibrahim Traoré has now led Burkina Faso for four years, the same length of time Thomas Sankara was in power. Both came to power as young, red-beret-wearing army captains, promising national sovereignty, Pan-Africanism and greater economic independence. Sankara, who seized power in 1983, launched what he called a “democratic and popular revolution,” promoting education, women’s empowerment, self-reliance and local production. He was assassinated in 1987. Nearly four decades later, Traoré says he is carrying Sankara’s torch forward but under very different conditions. His government has nationalised gold mines, promoted local industries and launched Faso Mebo, a major infrastructure programme aimed at building roads and developing cities using local resources. But the biggest difference is security. Burkina Faso remains under pressure from jihadist groups, with large parts of the country affected by violence and some towns facing blockades. title: Défense collective : Trois ans après, quels résultats pour l’AES ?
translated_title: Collective defence: Three years later, what results for the ESA?
excerpt: Trois ans après la signature de la Charte du Liptako-Gourma, la défense collective de l’Alliance des États du Sahel (AES) prend forme. Force unifiée, commandement commun et coopération opérationnelle en constituent les acquis. Leur efficacité reste difficile à apprécier. title: Niger Coup: Survival of the Military Regime and Growing Fragility
excerpt: The attempted coup in Niamey on the night of 28–29 August 2026 exposed a fundamental contradiction at the heart of General Abdourahamane Tiani’s rule. Although the regime survived its serious internal challenge since the July 2023 coup against Mohamed Bazoum, the episode revealed fractures within the armed forces, declining confidence in the government’s ability to improve security, and dependence on foreign military support. The episode demonstrated not simply regime resilience, but vulnerability. The rebellion was more serious than a limited mutiny. Rebels attacked the presidential palace, Air Base 101 at Diori Hamani Airport, and state television, and controlled the airport’s military complex for several hours. Participants reportedly included special-forces personnel with experience fighting in Tillabéri. The response revealed uncertainty within the wider army: some units hesitated, while one battalion reportedly refused to assault the base. Government forces ultimately retook Air Base 101 with assistance from the Russian Africa Corps, reportedly involving around 200 personnel. A

Although the regime survived its serious internal challenge since the July 2023 coup against Mohamed Bazoum, the episode revealed fractures within the armed forces, declining confidence in the government’s ability to improve security, and dependence on foreign military support.

title: Diplomatic Divide Threatens Sahel Security
excerpt: Nigeria’s northern states are experiencing a surge in terrorism spreading from the Sahel as strained diplomatic relations with Niger’s ruling junta complicates cross-border security. Tensions between the two countries began after the 2023 coup that overthrew Niger’s democratically elected president, Mohamed Bazoum. The situation worsened when Niger joined Burkina Faso and Mali in the Alliance of Sahelian States (AES) and withdrew from the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) in 2025. It later exited the Multinational Joint Task Force (MNJTF), which confronts terrorism in the Lake Chad Basin. After withdrawing from ECOWAS, Niger and its AES allies have repeatedly denounced their southern neighbors — with a special focus on Nigeria — for allegedly meddling in their internal affairs and attempting to destabilize their governments. According to reliable sources, a dispute over a piece of land in his Wawa community, in Borgu Kingdom, New Bussa Local Government Area allegedly led to sporadic shootings by a military task force which accidentally hit him, leading to the cause of his death. title: Panique à Sosso-Koïra : des munitions explosent lors d’un feu de débris
translated_title: Panic in Sosso-Koira: Ammunition explodes during a debris fire
excerpt: À Gao, une série d’explosions a semé la panique samedi 19 septembre dans le quartier de Sosso-Koïra. Un habitant avait mis le feu aux débris de son ancien hangar, ignorant que des munitions et deux grenades s’y trouvaient. Sous l’effet de la chaleur, plusieurs munitions ont explosé, provoquant l’inquiétude des riverains. Les forces de sécurité, rapidement intervenues, ont sécurisé le matériel restant qui n’avait pas explosé.
translated_excerpt: In Gao, a series of explosions caused panic on Saturday 19 September in the Sosso-Koïra district. A resident had set fire to the debris of his old hangar, unaware that ammunition and two grenades were there. Under the effect of the heat, several munitions exploded, causing concern among local residents. The security forces, quickly intervened, secured the remaining material that had not exploded.

title: Sécurité : Un drone ukrainien abattu par les forces spéciales maliennes au nord de Dioura
translated_title: Security: A Ukrainian drone shot down by Malian special forces north of Dioura
excerpt: Sécurité : Un drone ukrainien abattu par les forces spéciales maliennes au nord de Dioura Dans le cadre de leurs missions régaliennes de surveillance et de sécurisation du territoire national, les Forces armées maliennes (FAMa) ont abattu un drone de fabrication ukrainienne, samedi 19 septembre 2026 à 17h30. L’engin a été intercepté et neutralisé par les forces spéciales à environ 5 kilomètres au nord de la localité de Dioura, dans la région de Mopti. Selon les informations disponibles, les opérations de ratissage et de sécurisation se poursuivent activement dans le secteur afin de neutraliser toute menace résiduelle et de consolider la maîtrise du terrain. T.Sindy/Malijet.com
translated_excerpt: Security: A Ukrainian drone shot down by Malian special forces north of Dioura As part of their sovereign missions to monitor and secure the national territory, the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa) shot down a Ukrainian-made drone on Saturday, September 19, 2026 at 5:30 p.m. . The craft was intercepted and neutralized by special forces about 5 kilometers north of the locality of Dioura, in the Mopti region. According to available information, sweeping and securing operations are actively continuing in the area in order to neutralize any residual threat and consolidate control of the terrain. T.Sindy/Malijet.com
article_summary: As part of their sovereign missions to monitor and secure the national territory, the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa) shot down a Ukrainian-made drone on Saturday, September 19, 2026 at 5:30 p.m. . The craft was intercepted and neutralized by special forces about 5 kilometers north of the locality of Dioura, in the Mopti region.

La première promotion de cette école compte 15 lieutenants-colonels burkinabè. C’est en cela que le chef du gouvernement établit le rapport entre cette initiative et la souveraineté nationale. « On ne peut parler de souveraineté en matière de défense et de sécurité tant que nous allons continuer à envoyer notre élite militaire en formation ailleurs », a-t-il déclaré. Ces abus atroces et répétés par les deux camps témoignent de l’étendue et de l’intensification des violences qui s’opèrent depuis 2016, date du début des insurrections djihadistes dans le pays, dans un contexte général de dégradation de la s

title: Burkina Faso: People caught in a perfect storm of conflict, displacement and food insecurity
excerpt: Alongside the release of the world's most neglected displacement crises in 2022 and the 2023 Global Report on Internal Displacement, the Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) and the Internal Displacement Monitoring Center (IDMC) have worked together to identify the crucial yet often overlooked link between conflict, displacement and food security in Burkina Faso. For over a year, around 350,000 individuals have been trapped in Djibo, a city located in Burkina Faso's Sahel region. Among them, three-quarters are internally displaced people seeking refuge from the storms of conflict. Since February 2022, non-state armed groups have blockaded the city, planting explosives on roads and destroying critical infrastructure including bridges, water points and phone installations. Once a vibrant hub of trade and agriculture, Djibo is now cut off from the world. Fields lie abandoned, and food production has plummeted. Escalating prices have left many grappling with hunger, with some forced to resort to desperate measures such as eating leaves. Military convoys attempting to resupply Djibo residents
